name: Quantitative and Chemical Biology (QCB) PhD
summary: Vanderbilt PhD in quantitative and chemical biology. First-year students do four 2-month research rotations with faculty across participating departments before choosing a lab.

deadlines.label: Priority deadline
deadlines.note: Complete applications submitted by November 15 get early review. The Fall 2027 application opens August 1; the page prints no year for the date and gives no time.

deadlines.label: Final deadline
deadlines.note: The page says midnight on December 1, Central Standard Time (UTC-6). That could mean the start or end of December 1, so this shows the earlier one; finishing by the end of November 30 is safest.

timeline.interviews: Invitations go out on a rolling basis, typically by the end of February; if you have not received one by March 15 you are not being considered. Interviews are in person in Nashville, with a virtual option for those who cannot travel.
timeline.decisions: Admitted candidates have until April 15 to decide.

english.note: Required of international applicants and of those from non-English degree-granting institutions, unless waived; scores must be received by the deadline.

applicationFee.note: Anyone who has done research funded by a U.S. entity gets an automatic waiver, whatever their citizenship. Need-based waivers are only for U.S. citizens and permanent residents; a small number of other waivers go to international applicants based on qualifications.

documents: CV or resume, plus the application's Experiences tab
Transcripts (unofficial accepted; official only when requested)
requirements.note: You do not need a faculty sponsor to apply. Interfolio letters are not accepted. GRE scores older than five years are not accepted.

funding.note: Plus a $2,000 relocation bonus, 100% of tuition, and health coverage, dental and a yearly eye exam. International students get the same package; first-year funding is guaranteed as long as the student makes good progress, and second-year funding for international students comes through the BRET office.
